::: {.callout-note title="Practice entry, written in hindsight" icon=false}
This entry was written in November 2026, after the outcome was known, to
practise the journal's method on a past market day. The prediction shows what
the mechanism would have implied that evening. It is not part of the scored
record.
:::

## Observation
<!-- REWRITE: compare this day with July 29. What is the same chain running in reverse? -->

- SPY +1.80% to a record, QQQ +3.40%.
- Oil -5.7% to $75.77 on hopes of a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. TLT +0.77%.
- SPCX +9.43% to $125.33 before its first earnings report, due after the close.

## Mechanism
<!-- REWRITE: why does a rally BEFORE earnings make a good report less rewarding? -->

- Market: the risk-free rate channel. Lower oil, lower inflation pressure, lower yields, so stocks and bonds rose together.
- SpaceX: positioning. Buyers bid the stock up 9% before knowing the numbers.
- That raised the bar: the report now had to beat the higher expectation built into the price.

## Prediction
<!-- REWRITE: what did the Meta result on July 30 already teach about spending surprises? -->

- 55% probability that SPCX closes lower on August 5 than $125.33.
- Reasoning: a large run-up into an event leaves little room for a good result, and capital spending had just punished Meta.
- Wrong if SPCX closes above $125.33 on August 5.

## Scoring

- **Right.** SPCX fell 13.6% the next day: revenue beat expectations but capital spending rose sharply.
- Over five trading days, though, SPCX was up 6.4%.
- Lesson: the horizon is part of the prediction. The same view was right at one day and wrong at five.
